name: Diamonds, Hoops and Gridirons: America at Play
description: Baseball, basketball, American football and hockey: how a country invented sports, built leagues, broke colour lines and made stars like Ruth, Jordan and Serena.

checkpoints.name: Games before leagues
checkpoints.note: Lacrosse, a game with Native American roots, is already being played when settlers arrive. The Knickerbockers write down baseball rules in 1845, the America's Cup yacht race begins in 1851, and in 1869 Rutgers and Princeton play an early game of American football.

checkpoints.name: New games for new cities
checkpoints.note: Ice hockey is first played indoors in Montreal in 1875. The Brooklyn Dodgers form in 1884, James Naismith invents basketball in 1891 and volleyball follows in 1895. The Boston Marathon starts in 1897, and in 1912 Jim Thorpe wins Olympic gold medals, while Babe Ruth begins his baseball career.

checkpoints.name: Big leagues
checkpoints.note: Babe Ruth becomes baseball's first superstar. The National Basketball Association is founded in 1946, Jackie Robinson plays for the Dodgers in 1947 and breaks baseball's colour line, and the Dodgers leave Brooklyn after the 1957 season.

checkpoints.name: Television and superstars
checkpoints.note: The first Super Bowl in 1967 starts a television spectacle. Muhammad Ali and Billie Jean King become voices beyond sport, the Miracle on Ice of 1980 thrills a nation, and Michael Jordan and Wayne Gretzky begin careers that make basketball and hockey global.

checkpoints.name: Global stars
checkpoints.note: LeBron James becomes a leading scorer in the NBA, Tiger Woods and Serena Williams dominate golf and tennis, and Simone Biles reshapes gymnastics. American sport is now a worldwide stage, and the NBA draws players from every continent.
